newsitem.title: USA: PEPCO shuts Md. powr unit after bomb scare.
newsitem.headline: PEPCO shuts Md. powr unit after bomb scare.

text.p: Potomac Electric Power Co (PEPCO) shut a 312 megawatt (MW) coal-fired generating unit at its Chalk Point facility in Aquasco, Md., after a bomb scare earlier Thursday, said company spokeswoman Nancy Moses.
She did not have a restart date for the unit, adding the Chalk Point 1 unit was operating only at minimal power before the incident.
The other three Chalk Point generating units were not in operation for either economic reasons or seasonal maintenance.

Meanwhile, the county's fire department received a phone call in regard to a bomb on site at 0630 EDT. Fire officials searched the facility, and discovered nothing. The event was declared over at approximately 1100 EDT, Moses said.
During the bomb search, PEPCO evacuated onsite personnel, but only the plant's operators have since returned to the site, said Moses.
The incident did not affect power supply to its customers, she said. "We have enough generating capacity at low cost to meet our customer needs," she added.

Based in Washington, DC, Potomac Electric is the operator and sole owner of the Chalk Point complex, which has a total installed generating capacity of more than 2,000 MW. Units 1 and 2 burn primarily coal, and units 3 and 4 burn fuel oil.
